title: Resilient Logger Fault Bench
creator: Hank R. & Claude Code
subject: Environmental Monitoring
description: Five logger loops running the same read-and-append cycle against one shared fault timeline, each producing its own data file, log file and end-of-run verdict, plus a learner-configured fifth strategy.

learningObjectives: Critique four error-handling strategies against injected faults.
Judge which strategy preserves both the data and the ability to explain it later.
Explain why a bare except is worse than no handling at all.
Identify which exception types a handler must catch to survive a given fault.
prerequisites: Chapter 13: exception handling and the logger loop
Chapter 12: what an OSError from an I2C read means

keyQuestions: Which matters more, a logger that never stops or a logger that records why it stopped?
What happens when you press Ctrl-C on a logger with a bare except?
How would you tell, six months later, whether a gap was weather or a bug?
Can the code inside an except block fail?
commonMisconceptions: Any try/except is better than none.
except: pass makes a program robust.
A logger that keeps running has not lost anything.
An exception handler cannot itself raise an exception.
assessmentOpportunities: Records the outcome of one fault across all five strategies and explains the differences.
Explains the KeyboardInterrupt case in their own words.
Configures a fifth logger that matches or beats the recommended pattern on both criteria.
